anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L1 task has a simplified mine surface but still uses a projected 3D block scene, raycast mining, blockers, lava/support hazards and durability. Firewatch d1 has less continuous aiming and no 3D depth, but it already requires several dependent cell moves, ladder legality, one blocked fire and an exact resident position. Firewatch d4 is clearly above this low-end direct-target task in route-state bookkeeping, while the comparison does not establish an absolute level for every Firewatch profile.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L2 task is a one-target search: cursor proximity reveals the target among noise and decoys, followed by one click within a tolerance. Firewatch d2 and above require a multi-action route whose legal moves and available fire actions depend on the current cell, facing, face and cleared-fire set. Firewatch has much less cursor precision, but materially more dependent planning than this one-shot L2 task.

evidence.explanation: The approved L2 baseline is full and its d2 profile exposes decoys, visual noise and a single accepted click radius.

Firewatch changes facing and position through walls, fires, ladders and face seams, and changes inventory when a fire is cleared.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L3 task has three ordered lamps, walls and wells, continuous momentum and collision recovery; its full surface is an analog drag and its grader replays every physics tick. Firewatch d4 has no analogous motor precision or continuous physics, but it replaces that burden with a larger two-face discrete route, ladder choices, fire inventory and map recall. It is plausibly at or above the L3 planning burden, but the different control demands make the L3/L4 boundary uncertain.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: Both approved L4 Blind Dice and Firewatch d4 are multi-step navigation tasks with state-dependent moves and a full keyboard surface. Blind Dice additionally hides die orientation between sparse scanners, requires ordered gate crossings and replays orientation/path ledgers. Firewatch exposes the inspected face map and permits a guaranteed one-fire alternate route; its d4 is therefore less constrained and less hidden-state-heavy, but its two-face, six-floor map and fire/ladder route choices keep it in the same broad upper-mid range.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L5 task has four state-changing swaps: each accepted swap changes the later board, cascades/refills affect the next decision, exact score and move count matter, and a forbidden cell can terminate the run. Firewatch's geometry is generated once, movement is a discrete replay, and the grader accepts any resident-reaching route with nonnegative stock; even d5 therefore lacks the L5 anchor's exact changing-board constraint.

visible_baseline_solution: A normal screenshot-only solution reads the currently displayed face map, presses the eye to inspect the other face, and keeps enough of the two maps to choose a legal route from the start to the resident. It moves horizontally one cell at a time, crosses to the other face only by walking past an edge, and climbs or descends only where the visible ladder rule permits. When the next cell is an active fire, the first move toward it establishes the facing and remains blocked; the solver then uses Shift and repeats the same move to enter the cleared cell. It continues until the exact resident cell is occupied and presses CERTIFY RESCUE. The browser records each move, blocked outcome, inspection, fire clear, before/after snapshot and final state; the grader requires a sequential internally consistent transcript, the correct input source, the resident position, completed=true, at least one move and nonnegative stock. Discrete buttons or keys provide the movement, so no drag or pixel-aim tolerance is part of the baseline control problem.

baseline_judgment.rationale: Keep the d4/full assignment provisionally. It is materially above the approved L1 and L2 tasks in dependent route state, map recall and multi-action planning; it is plausibly at or above the approved L3 board's planning burden; and it is near the approved L4 Blind Dice task in overall navigation scale. Firewatch is weaker than Blind Dice in hidden orientation, ordered gates and strict route ledgers, and is clearly below the approved L5 changing-board exact-score task. That makes d4 a defensible upper-mid placement, but source inspection cannot resolve the L3/L4 cross-mechanic boundary or substitute for calibration.

findings.claim: The controls field 'inspection_complexity' is present in every difficulty profile but is not an active difficulty parameter.
findings.causal_explanation: The generator reads the numeric tower parameters and never branches on inspection_complexity. The browser always provides the same eye button and renders the selected opposite face with the same information structure, so the repeated value cannot distinguish adjacent profiles.

evidence.explanation: Every profile sets inspection_complexity to the identical value both_faces.
The generator extracts floor, width, ladder, fire, decoy, wall and seam values but does not read inspection_complexity.

findings.recommended_action: Remove the unsupported field from the profile knob set or implement a visibly different inspection rule before crediting it in difficulty comparisons.

findings.claim: The nominal route_fire_count is not a minimum required fire-clearing count: every generated profile is designed with a one-fire alternate route, while the grader accepts any resident-reaching replay with nonnegative stock.
findings.causal_explanation: The generator deliberately places a fire cut and reserves an alternate path that clears exactly one fire, while the canonical route consumes the nominal stock. The grader does not require the canonical route, a seam count, an inspection or use of all stock. Thus higher nominal stock values mostly increase route-choice/clutter structure; they do not force four or five extinguisher decisions in the d4/d5 task.

evidence.explanation: The generator comment and construction explicitly promise a one-fire alternate and a canonical route using nominal stock.
The alternate path is checked after wall placement and must remain valid with all but its one alternate fire blocked.
The hidden resource contract records alternate and minimum route clears as one while separately recording the nominal canonical count.
The pass condition checks the final resident position, completion and nonnegative stock, not a prescribed route or fire-clear count.

findings.recommended_action: Treat route_fire_count as nominal stock and route-choice structure in the audit. If the intended difficulty requires scaling mandatory resource decisions, add source-backed route-cost grading or remove that claim from the profile descriptions; calibrate before changing labels.

findings.claim: Inspecting both faces is an efficient planning aid but is not a graded success requirement.
findings.causal_explanation: The browser records INSPECT and the grader reports inspection_count, but the pass expression never checks it. A transcript can therefore be accepted without an INSPECT event if the route is discovered or executed by other visible feedback. The practical solvability of a no-inspection route is a runtime/calibration question, but the absence of a requirement is source-proven.

evidence.explanation: The eye action is optional in the browser event model and only changes the inspected face.
The grader counts inspections but does not make an inspection event part of the replay contract's required actions.
The pass expression omits inspection_count, canonical route, seam count and fire-clear quota.

findings.recommended_action: Do not describe inspection as mandatory in the difficulty rationale unless calibration shows it is practically necessary. If it is intended as a required mechanic, add a source-backed requirement or retain the current caveat.

concise_summary: Firewatch Fold d4/full is a plausible upper-mid discrete route-planning task: it is above the approved low-end target tasks in dependent map state, comparable in broad scale to Blind Dice Courier L4, and below Exact-Change Candy Cascade L5's changing-board exact constraint. Keep the baseline provisionally, but do not credit the inactive inspection_complexity field or treat nominal fire stock as a mandatory number of clears.
limitations: This is source analysis only; no browser, benchmark evaluation, multi-seed generation, human/VNC run or agent calibration was performed.
No historical pre-controls implementation or fixed-seed artifact was available, so historical preservation is unknown.
The absolute L3/L4 placement and the d5/L5 comparison remain uncertain without comparable solve-time and error measurements.
